nodes.label: Confidence Calibration Requires Exact (engine, model, version, corpus) Match
nodes.rationale: Raw model confidence is not comparable across engines/models/versions, and the project refuses to make an unearned accuracy claim, so calibration only applies on an exact four-field match.
nodes.norm_label: confidence calibration requires exact (engine, model, version, corpus) match

nodes.label: Exactly One Processing Engine, Never Auto-Routed
nodes.rationale: Users need explicit visibility into whether document content stays local or goes to a specific cloud provider, for privacy/compliance reasons; an automatic engine-routing heuristic would make the data path implicit, conflicting with the project's privacy stance.
nodes.norm_label: exactly one processing engine, never auto-routed

nodes.label: Local Layout Detection Precedes Ollama OCR Recognition
nodes.rationale: Family-native Ollama OCR models (GLM-OCR, PaddleOCR-VL, DeepSeek-OCR) are not reliably steerable into whole-page structured JSON with grounding, so PP-DocLayoutV3 detects regions on CPU first and each crop gets a family-specific native prompt instead.
nodes.norm_label: local layout detection precedes ollama ocr recognition

nodes.label: Why Explicit Providers, Not a Plugin Registry
nodes.norm_label: why explicit providers, not a plugin registry

nodes.label: No Plugin Registry or Auto-Discovery
nodes.rationale: Adding a provider means manually editing model_catalog.py and one if-branch in runtime.py's cloud_adapter(), preserving traceability from 'which provider ran' back to one visible, centrally-reviewed line of code, matching the project's 'never auto-route' philosophy.

nodes.label: No Shared Provider Base Class
nodes.rationale: Providers genuinely differ in behavior (Gemini's thinking-level mapping, ignored image detail parameter, xAI reusing the OpenAI shape with different flags, Ollama's chained composition); a shared base class would need enough hooks/overrides to cover every divergence before a fifth provider ships, making it an abstraction maintained for its own sake.

nodes.label: No LandingAI Parity or Accuracy Claim
nodes.rationale: The locked benchmark corpus is intentionally too small for a comparative claim; the project deliberately disclaims LandingAI ADE parity and refuses to publish a score without raw results and full provenance.
nodes.norm_label: no landingai parity or accuracy claim

nodes.label: Organize Determinism Design
nodes.rationale: Classify/Split/Section run as pure Python over an already-parsed ParseResponse with no model calls, so every output is traceable to a page/character range. This trades classification recall and semantic understanding for the guarantee that no output is hallucinated or non-reproducible; an LLM-based classifier was explicitly rejected because it would reintroduce exactly the unverifiable-answer risk Parse's grounding model exists to prevent.

nodes.label: Two-Export Contract Design
nodes.rationale: Keeping the ADE v2-style export and the Paperplane v5 export as two distinct, named contracts lets a consumer never guess which fields are the stable interop surface vs the Paperplane extension surface; a single merged schema would either bloat the interop-facing shape or force richer data to be reconstructed from a flatter representation. The split also lets Paperplane be explicit that 'ADE-compatible' means contract-shape and job-semantics compatibility, not API or accuracy parity with LandingAI.
